question: Which organisation initiated a 12-day cybersecurity exercise called ‘Cyber Suraksha’, starting 16 June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Defence Cyber Agency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Defence Cyber Agency (DCyA)** initiated a comprehensive **12-day** cybersecurity exercise titled **‘Cyber Suraksha’**, which commenced on **16 June 2025**.
 
• The exercise is designed to evaluate and enhance the **cyber-defence readiness** and operational capabilities of the **Indian Armed Forces** in the face of evolving digital threats.
 
• The **‘Cyber Suraksha’** exercise serves as a collaborative platform for the **Indian Army**, **Indian Navy**, and **Indian Air Force** to develop **jointness** and **synergy** in their cyber operations.
 
• A primary objective of this drill is to test the robustness of the **military’s information technology infrastructure** and ensure the security of **strategic communication networks** against potential **cyber-espionage** and **state-sponsored attacks**.
 
• By conducting this exercise, the **DCyA** aims to refine **Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)** and strengthen the nation's **cyber-resilience** within the framework of the **Ministry of Defence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Cyber Agency (DCyA):**
 
 
• The **DCyA** is a tri-service command of the **Indian Armed Forces**, established in **2019** to handle **cyber warfare** and **digital security**.
 
• It is headquartered in **New Delhi** and operates under the administrative and operational control of the **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)**.
 
• The agency was formed based on the recommendations of the **Naresh Chandra Task Force** to integrate the disparate cyber capabilities of the three services into a single unified command.
 
• It plays a vital role in protecting **critical information infrastructure (CII)** and conducting both **offensive and defensive cyber operations** to safeguard national interests.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Cyber Exercises:**
 
 
• In the modern era of **Hybrid Warfare**, the **cyber domain** is recognized as the **fifth dimension of warfare**, alongside land, air, sea, and space.
 
• Exercises like **‘Cyber Suraksha’** are crucial for identifying vulnerabilities in **military hardware** and software systems, including **Satellite-based communication** and **C4I systems**.
 
• These drills ensure that the **defence personnel** are well-trained in the latest **encryption techniques** and **threat-hunting methodologies**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inter-Agency Cooperation:** The **Indian Defence Cyber Agency** works in close coordination with national bodies such as **CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team)** and the **National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC)**.
 
• **Technological Focus:** The exercise focuses on emerging technologies such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Machine Learning (ML)**, and **Quantum Computing** to stay ahead of sophisticated **malware** and **ransomware** attacks.
 
• **Strategic Policy:** Such initiatives are aligned with India’s **National Cyber Security Strategy**, which emphasizes **atmanirbharta (self-reliance)** in developing indigenous **cyber-security tools** and software.
 
• **Historical Context:** Since its inception in **2019**, the **DCyA** has significantly expanded its footprint, conducting multiple training programs and drills to secure the **digital ecosystem** of the **Indian Ministry of Defence**.
